column1: # Canonical definition of the integration suite set.
# This file is the single source of truth for what an integration run is
# expected to observe. scripts/test-integration.sh derives expected,
# attempted, completed and every per-unit status from it -- there is no
# second list and no hand-maintained counter anywhere. Adding a suite here
# is the only step required to make it part of the expected set.
#   id          stable identifier, appears in the evidence manifest
#   modes       comma-separated run modes that select this unit
#   depends_on  unit ids this one needs, or "-"
#   command     shell command; $compose_run expands to the compose runner
# depends_on is declared but empty for every unit in V1, and that is a
# finding rather than an omission: every integration suite applies the
# migrations it needs (verified: all of them call runner.Up), and the CLI
# smoke bootstraps its own state (migrate up, registry sync, its own task
# fixtures). The apparent "platform/postgres must run first" relationship
# was positional, not real. Schema bootstrap is now an explicit
# precondition instead, so a suite failing here blocks nothing.
# cli-smoke is deliberately one unit in V1. It is a 239-line single shell
# invocation; splitting it into individually observable assertions is a
# separate front, tracked as debt. Modelling it as one unit is honest --
# the harness reports exactly the granularity it can actually observe.
# and the three executive-* units below were real, passing (or, for
# executive-postgres, one known pre-existing failure -- see its own
# handoff entry) integration suites that this manifest never listed.
# COMPLETE_GREEN never depended on observing them; a control could live
# entirely inside one of these packages and be invisible to the official
# harness. This file being the single source of truth (see the file
# header) is exactly what makes adding four lines the whole fix.
